source.trial: COPERNICUS (severe HF, n=1156 vs 1133), label section 5.3
source.citation: COREG (carvedilol) FDA label, DailyMed set id 07c619c6-4a0c-445e-94fa-664a54f68a39, section 5.3 (Hypotension); Table 1 in section 6.1 shown in the notes

caveats: The carvedilol label gives two figures for fainting (syncope) in the same trial of severe heart failure (COPERNICUS). Section 5.3 says syncope occurred in 2.9% of patients on carvedilol against 2.3% on placebo. The label's adverse-event table lists 8% against 5%. This tool uses 2.9% against 2.3%, an excess of 0.6 points.

Why that one: section 5.3 is the label's dedicated statement of this event, with one decimal place, while the table counts adverse events of any cause rounded to whole percents and lists only events that were more frequent on the drug. The label's other heart failure figures agree with the lower figure (3.4% against 2.5% in mild to moderate heart failure, section 5.3). Using 8% against 5% would charge an excess of 3.0 points, five times as much.
CAPRICORN (after myocardial infarction) gave 3.9% against 1.9%; it is another population and is not used. Median exposure was 10.4 months, so the figures are used as observed, not scaled to a year.
rows.population: COPERNICUS severe HF (carvedilol n=1156, placebo n=1133; median exposure 10.4 months)
rows.definition_used: Syncope (label section 5.3)
rows.quote: COREG label section 5.3: "In a long-term, placebo-controlled trial in severe heart failure (COPERNICUS), hypotension and postural hypotension occurred in 15.1% and syncope in 2.9% of heart failure subjects receiving COREG compared with 8.7% and 2.3% of placebo subjects, respectively." Table 1 (section 6.1), severe HF, COREG vs placebo (%): Syncope 8 vs 5.
rows.notes: Controller ruling 2026-11-19 (round 1 review, E6): the label gives two placebo-controlled heart failure figures for syncope that disagree. Table 1 (adverse events regardless of causality, incidence above 3%, integer percentages): severe heart failure (COPERNICUS) COREG 8% vs placebo 5%; mild-to-moderate heart failure (U.S. trials, n = 765 vs 437) 3% vs 3%. Section 5.3 (hypotension): COPERNICUS syncope 2.9% vs 2.3%; primarily mild-to-moderate heart failure 3.4% vs 2.5%. (CAPRICORN, after myocardial infarction, 3.9% vs 1.9%, is another population and is not used.) CHOSEN: COPERNICUS 2.9% vs 2.3% from section 5.3, an excess of 0.6 points. By the table's own source rule (fixed definition first, heart failure before other populations, placebo-controlled, then more patients, then longer follow-up, never by the result): both candidates are placebo-controlled in heart failure; COPERNICUS (2,289 patients) has more patients than the mild-to-moderate trials (1,202); between the two COPERNICUS figures the section 5.3 statement is the label's dedicated, one-decimal statement of syncope, whereas Table 1 is an any-cause adverse-event table rounded to whole percents (8 vs 5 could be 7.5-8.5 vs 4.5-5.5) that lists only events more frequent with drug. The same trial gives 3.0 in one table and 0.6 in the other; the earlier row charged 3.0 (Table 1) and did not mention section 5.3, so it charged about five times the rate. Follow-up: median exposure 10.4 months = 0.867 year, not above one year, so the figures are used as observed (2.9 - 2.3 = 0.6).

rows.notes: Controller ruling 2026-11-19 (round 1 review, E6): the label gives two placebo-controlled heart failure figures for syncope that disagree. Table 1 (adverse events regardless of causality, incidence above 3%, integer percentages): severe heart failure (COPERNICUS) COREG 8% vs placebo 5%; mild-to-moderate heart failure (U.S. trials, n = 765 vs 437) 3% vs 3%. Section 5.3 (hypotension): COPERNICUS syncope 2.9% vs 2.3%; primarily mild-to-moderate heart failure 3.4% vs 2.5%. (CAPRICORN, after myocardial infarction, 3.9% vs 1.9%, is another population and is not used.) CHOSEN: COPERNICUS 2.9% vs 2.3% from section 5.3, an excess of 0.6 points. By the table's own source rule (fixed definition first, heart failure before other populations, placebo-controlled, then more patients, then longer follow-up, never by the result): both candidates are placebo-controlled in heart failure; COPERNICUS (2,289 patients) has more patients than the mild-to-moderate trials (1,202); between the two COPERNICUS figures the section 5.3 statement is the label's dedicated, one-decimal statement of syncope, whereas Table 1 is an any-cause adverse-event table rounded to whole percents (8 vs 5 could be 7.5-8.5 vs 4.5-5.5) that lists only events more frequent with drug. The same trial gives 3.0 in one table and 0.6 in the other; the earlier row charged 3.0 (Table 1) and did not mention section 5.3, so it charged about five times the rate. Follow-up: median exposure 10.4 months = 0.867 year, not above one year, so the figures are used as observed (2.9 - 2.3 = 0.6). Carvedilol's COPERNICUS figure is used as the beta-blocker sibling for metoprolol succinate and bisoprolol.
